errors.problem: On the khāʾ card, the khāʾ page and the khayr/ghayr minimal pair, خَيْر is taught as 'good' / 'goodness' (example.en: good; pairs[0][0].en: goodness). The tap still carries a scenario remark, 'good night', which خَيْر alone never means (and صَبَاح/مَسَاء الْخَيْر are good morning/evening). Reported in rounds 1 and 2, still present (glossary/auto.json: "خَيْر").
errors.alsoChange: fix in these three lessons (or the plain gloss for خَيْر), not as a scenario-specific sense

errors.problem: On the nūn card and the vowels page نُور is the example word 'light' (example.en: light), but the tap shows only the girl's name. Round 3 introduced two-reading glosses for words that are both a name and a common word; this one still shows only the name. Reported in rounds 1 and 2, still present.

In the diphthong diagram 'fatha + وْ = aw', وْ is the letter wāw with sukūn (the second half of the glide aw), not the conjunction 'and'. Its neighbour يْ is correctly glossed 'the letter yāʾ'. Reported in round 2, still present (glossary/auto.json: "وْ": "and").
errors.fix: وْ=the letter wāw (with sukūn: the glide aw)

notes.note: رَقْم (raqm) for 'number' is correct MSA (Hans Wehr: raqm, pl. arqām) and used consistently across the course; رَقَم (raqam) is also widely heard. Not an error, just checked.

The waṣl page teaches the shortened 'fi l-madīna' / 'ila l-yamīn' / 'fi l-bayt', but the ⟶ lines show 'Fī l-madīna', 'Ilā l-yamīn', 'Fī l-bayt', so the tip reads 'fī l-madīna is fi l-madīna'. ALA-LC house style, but on this page it looks like a contradiction; consider a page-level note or leaving prose untransliterated.

Where the prose already gives the transliteration next to the Arabic, the ⟶ line doubles it: 'ṭālib (ṭālib)', 'dhahabtu (dhahabtu)', 'bayt bayt, house', 'al-qamar → al-qamar', 'ʿani l-fīlm (ʿani l-fīlm)'. Harmless but noisy.
الْقَاهِرَةِ taps to 'Cairo; Cairo (city in Egypt)' (duplicated sense), and its ⟶ is lower-case 'fī l-qāhirati' while [28].pairs[0][1] gives 'Mina l-Qāhira'. Cosmetic.
Now 'pulled up and back towards the throat' (round-2 fix applied). Acceptable; 'raised towards the soft palate and pulled back' would match the emphatics/ṭāʾ/ḍād pages word for word.
'نِهَايَة is said nihāya' illustrates nothing because the Arabic is written without tanwīn; the diagram's 'nihāyatun → nihāya' makes the point. Could write نِهَايَةٌ in the tip.
سَتَأْتِي is also 'you (m.) will come'; glossed only 'she will come', matching the page's English. Not an error.

summary: Checked the whole export (1,892 lines): all 31 letter cards (char, name, Arabic name, transliteration, IPA, sun/moon status, sound tip, example) and all 30 pronunciation pages (titles, tips, diagrams, errors, examples, minimal pairs). 299 Arabic strings checked (char/letters/nameAr/examples/pairs), 0 with wrong Arabic: letter names, IPA, the 14/14 sun/moon split, minimal pairs, stress rules, helping-vowel rules (mina, ʿani, humu), pausal forms and case-ending rules are correct, and the round-2 fixes (حَارّ, the -u tap, the ṣād diagram, السَّفَر, حَجَزَ) are in. 501 tap glosses checked (on 373 tap lines), 6 wrong across 3 words (خَيْر x3 'good night', نُور x2 name only, وْ 'and'), all reported in earlier rounds and still present. 374 ⟶ lines checked: two engine problems with bare letters in prose — a regression where a bracketed bare letter in a title now prints '()' (12 titles + 1 diagram; jīm still 'J'), and the unnamed hamza seats. Total 5 errors, 0 major, 5 minor.
